import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/button.tokens.json";

import * as ButtonStories from "./Button.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={ButtonStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={ButtonStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Button to start an action, submit a form, or change the state of the interface.

### When not to use

Don’t use a Button to navigate to another page.
Use a [Standalone Link](/docs/components-navigation-standalone-link--docs) or a [Call to Action Link](/docs/components-navigation-call-to-action-link--docs) instead, or an inline [Link](/docs/components-navigation-link--docs) in running text.

### How to use

Use only one primary Button per screen.
The primary variant draws attention to the most important action; multiple primaries dilute that signal.

Set `type="submit"` to make the Button submit the surrounding form.

Wrap two or more Buttons or links that sit next to each other in an [Action Group](/docs/components-layout-action-group--docs).

Always provide a short, descriptive label that names the action.
For icon-only Buttons, supply the label through the `children` prop – it is read by screen readers even though it is not shown.

### How to write

Write a short label that names the action.
Use the verb's infinitive form in Dutch, e.g. 'Verwijderen' or 'Opslaan', not 'Verwijder' or 'Sla op'.
Avoid generic labels like 'Klik hier' or 'OK'.

## Examples

### Primary

A primary Button draws attention to the most important call to action.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Primary} />

### Secondary

Use a secondary Button for other actions.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Secondary} />

### Tertiary

Tertiary Buttons distinguish themselves from secondary Buttons when even less emphasis is needed.
They are also the choice for icon-only Buttons.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Tertiary} />

### With icon

Add an icon if it makes the Button’s purpose easier or faster to recognise.
The icon appears after the label by default.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.WithIcon} />

### With icon before

The icon can also appear before the label.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.WithIconBefore} />

### With icon only

A Button can consist of just an icon, but only one of our [functional icons](/docs/brand-assets-icons--docs#functional-icons).
You must still provide a label for screen reader users.
If the icon-only Button must align with surrounding text, use an [Icon Button](/docs/components-buttons-icon-button--docs) instead.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.WithIconOnly} />

### Text wrapping

The label may wrap over multiple lines when no shorter text is available, when two Buttons sit next to each other on a narrow screen, or when the user has configured a large font on their device.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.TextWrapping} />

## Features

The Button handles its own focus, hover, active, and disabled states.
On narrow screens or with longer labels, it wraps text without losing alignment.

## Design

The three variants form a hierarchy of importance: primary, secondary, tertiary.
This lets a screen present one clear focal action without ranking every other Button against it.

The icon size stays constant regardless of the label length, so a row of Buttons aligns visually even when their text differs.

## See also

- [Icon Button](/docs/components-buttons-icon-button--docs) – an icon-only button aligned with surrounding text.
- [Standalone Link](/docs/components-navigation-standalone-link--docs) – for navigation to another page.
- [Call to Action Link](/docs/components-navigation-call-to-action-link--docs) – a prominent link styled like a Button.
- [Action Group](/docs/components-layout-action-group--docs) – lays out multiple Buttons and links.
- [Prose](/docs/utilities-css-prose--docs) – applies the recommended vertical spacing for editorial content.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Choose an Icon Button instead of a regular Button when it must align with text.
Match the size of the Icon Button to the surrounding text.

### When not to use

Only [functional icons](/docs/brand-assets-icons--docs#functional-icons) belong in an Icon Button.
For other icons, use a [Button](/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) so that the user can read its label.

### How to use

An Icon Button still needs a label for screen reader users.
Provide it through the `children` prop; it is read aloud even though it is not shown.

## Examples

### On a coloured background

An Icon Button on a coloured background must set [the correct text colour](/docs/brand-design-tokens-colour--docs#pairing-foreground-with-background-colours) to provide enough contrast.
We have light and dark background colours, and Icon Buttons behave differently on each.

#### Contrast colour

Use the contrast colour on a lime, orange or yellow background.
It will make the icon black.

<Canvas of={IconButtonStories.ContrastColour} />

#### Inverse colour

Use the inverse colour on an azure, blue, green, magenta or purple background.
It will make the icon white.

<Canvas of={IconButtonStories.InverseColour} />

## See also

- [Button](/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) – for actions that show a text label.
- [Icon](/docs/components-media-icon--docs) – a non-interactive icon.

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/accordion.tokens.json";

import * as AccordionStories from "./Accordion.stories.tsx";
import * as AccordionSectionStories from "./AccordionSection.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={AccordionStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={AccordionStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Subcomponents

### Section

Pairs a heading with collapsible content.
Use `defaultExpanded` to show the content initially.
Pass `onToggle` to be notified when the section opens or closes.

<Canvas of={AccordionSectionStories.Section} />

<Controls of={AccordionSectionStories.Section} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use an Accordion to keep secondary content collapsed by default, so the primary content of a page stays prominent.
A typical example is a list of frequently asked questions.

### When not to use

Don’t hide essential information in an Accordion.
Users may not realise it is there.

For long content that deserves its own page, split it across multiple pages instead.
That often improves both usability and findability through search engines.

### How to use

Use between 3 and 10 sections.
Fewer is rarely worth the extra interaction; more makes the list hard to scan.

Provide each section with a clear, descriptive label.
Users cannot scan the content inside a collapsed section.

Set `headingLevel` on the Accordion to match its position in the page hierarchy.
All sections share that level.

### How to write

Write labels that describe what the user will find inside the section.
Use sentence case.

## Examples

### Expanded by default

Pass `defaultExpanded` to a section to make it visible from the start.
Use this sparingly – it works against the goal of keeping content collapsed.

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.ExpandedByDefault} />

### Reduce landmarks

An Accordion Section renders a `<section>` element by default, which creates a landmark region.
Many landmarks on one page can be noisy for screen reader users.
For Accordions with six or more sections, render generic `<div>` elements through `sectionAs="div"`.

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.ReduceLandmarks} />

## Features

The Accordion provides the heading and the show-or-hide behaviour.
Section content can include formatted text, links, and other components.

### Keyboard navigation

| Key             | Behaviour                                                 |
| :-------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter or Space  | Open or close the focused section                         |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move to the next or previous focusable element            |
| Down / Up arrow | Move focus to the next or previous section (wraps around) |
| Home / End      | Move focus to the first or last section                   |

### Find in page

Browser ‘Find in page’ (Ctrl+F or ⌘+F) does not search inside collapsed sections.
If you can anticipate the search term, expand the relevant section automatically.

## Design

Section headings stay visible while their content collapses.
This lets users scan every section label without expanding anything.

Opening one section does not close the others.
A user looking for a specific answer can leave related context open as they explore.

## See also

- [Prose](/docs/utilities-css-prose--docs) – applies the recommended vertical spacing for editorial content.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Meta of={DialogStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={DialogStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Dialog for short and non-frequent tasks.

### When not to use

Use Dialogs sparingly because they interrupt the user’s workflow.
Consider using the main flow for regular tasks.

### How to use

To open the Dialog, use `Dialog.open(dialogId)` from the React package.
To close it, either call the `Dialog.close` function or add a `<form>` as in the ‘confirmation’ example.

Wrap multiple buttons in an [Action Group](/docs/components-layout-action-group--docs).

#### Focusing a specific element

When a Dialog opens (and no element has `autofocus`), the browser places focus on the first focusable element inside it.
In this component that is the close button, which is a safe default: the user can read the Dialog before acting.

To give another element the initial focus instead, add the `autofocus` attribute to it, or the `autoFocus` prop in React.
Use this for the single element you expect the user to act on first, such as a text field or the primary Button.

Moving the initial focus has risks, so choose that element with care:

- Focus that lands past the heading and body text can cause screen reader users to skip the explanation above it. Only move focus when one element clearly comes first.
- Don’t place focus on a destructive or irreversible action. A user confirming by reflex with Enter or Space could lose data. In the confirmation example below, focus the option that keeps the user’s data safe.
- On touchscreen devices, autofocus on a text field opens the on-screen keyboard immediately, which can hide part of the Dialog.

For more information: [MDN: the dialog element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog#accessibility).

## Examples

### Asking to confirm

Use a `form` when asking the user to confirm an action, e.g. through ‘OK’ and ‘Cancel’ buttons.
Add `method="dialog"` to make the browser close the Dialog when the form is submitted.
Wrap multiple Buttons in an [Action Group](/docs/components-layout-action-group--docs) and place it in the `footer`.
Add an `id` to the form and use it in the `form` attribute of the buttons.
Set a `value` on each button to identify which one was clicked.
Consult [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/dialog#handling_the_return_value_from_the_dialog) for more information.

<Canvas of={DialogStories.Confirmation} />

## Features

The Dialog is a [query container](/docs/utilities-css-query-container--docs) for inline size, so elements inside it can adapt their appearance to the width of the Dialog.

### Keyboard navigation

| Key         | Behaviour                                                        |
| :---------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab         | Moves focus to the next focusable element inside the Dialog.     |
| Shift + Tab | Moves focus to the previous focusable element inside the Dialog. |
| Escape      | Closes the Dialog.                                               |

## See also

- [Action Group](/docs/components-layout-action-group--docs) – lays out multiple Buttons.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

The Page component wraps the [Page Header](/docs/components-containers-page-header--docs), [Page Footer](/docs/components-containers-page-footer--docs), and the main content in between.
As a root layout component, it must be used for all websites for the City of Amsterdam.

## Examples

See the [Home Page](/story/pages-public-home-page--default) template for public websites for a full-page example.

### With menu

Internal websites can add a [Menu](/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) for navigating between its modules and pages.
This is an alternative to the approach using Link Lists, which is appropriate for public, content-oriented websites.

We can’t display the example here, as it requires Compact Mode to be enabled, which affects the example for the public Home Page template.
Open the [full example page](/story/components-containers-page--with-menu) or see the [Home Page](/story/pages-internal-home-page--default) template for internal websites.

## Features

The Page is a [query container](/docs/utilities-css-query-container--docs) for inline size, so elements inside it can adapt their appearance to the width of the page.
For elements inside a [Grid Cell](/docs/components-layout-grid--docs) or [Dialog](/docs/components-containers-dialog--docs), that nearer container takes precedence; the Page covers everything else.

## Design

The Page is centered horizontally and sets a maximum width of 90 rems (usually 1440 pixels).
With a Menu, that becomes 120 rems (1920 pixels).

## See also

- [Page Header](/docs/components-containers-page-header--docs) – sits at the top of the Page.
- [Page Footer](/docs/components-containers-page-footer--docs) – sits at the bottom of the Page.

<Meta of={PageFooterStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={PageFooterStories} />

<Primary />

This component has no props to configure.

## Subcomponents

The Spotlight subcomponent provides the blue area at the top of the Page Footer.
It has no props of its own; the example above shows it in place.

### Menu

Presents the links in the Spotlight.
Its visually hidden `heading` describes the menu for users of assistive technology.

<Canvas of={PageFooterMenuStories.Menu} />

<Controls of={PageFooterMenuStories.Menu} />

### Menu Link

Navigates to a page.
Set `linkComponent` to integrate with a routing library.

<Canvas of={PageFooterMenuLinkStories.MenuLink} />

<Controls of={PageFooterMenuLinkStories.MenuLink} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

The Page Footer must be used on all websites for the City of Amsterdam.
It must be the same on every page of the website.

### How to use

The content section is required for public websites, but not for internal ones.
It offers space for various practical links:

- The first column focuses on contact information.
  Make it specific and tailor it to the website or page.
- The second column contains links to other relevant sources.
- The third column refers to newsletters, events, social media, etc.

The menu is for links to privacy policies, cookie statements, and other information about the website itself.

Set [the inverse colour](/docs/brand-design-tokens-colour--docs#pairing-foreground-with-background-colours) on all text and links in this area.

If the Page Footer contains [Headings](/docs/components-text-heading--docs), give them level 2 and a size of 'level-3'.
A visually hidden heading to group them is not necessary – the footer's landmark provides enough guidance.

The menu includes a visually hidden heading for screen reader users.
The default heading text is 'Over deze website'.
Customize it when the menu serves a different purpose, or the interface language is not Dutch.

## Examples

### Onderzoek en Statistiek

The Page Footer for a specific website can be a bit different.
Here’s an example for the ‘Onderzoek en Statistiek’ department.

<Canvas of={PageFooterStories.OnderzoekEnStatistiek} />

### Custom menu heading

For an English website, update the visually hidden heading to ‘Support links’.
If your website is in Dutch, but the default heading of ‘Over deze website’ doesn’t reflect the content of the menu, choose a different heading as well.

<Canvas of={PageFooterStories.CustomMenuHeading} />

- [Page](/docs/components-containers-page--docs) – contains the Page Footer.
- [Page Header](/docs/components-containers-page-header--docs) – sits at the top of the Page.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";

import * as PageHeaderMenuLinkStories from "./PageHeaderMenuLink.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={PageHeaderStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={PageHeaderStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Subcomponents

The Grid Cell Narrow Window Only subcomponent accepts all Grid Cell props and is only displayed in narrow windows.
The primary example uses it to repeat a menu link below the header.

### Menu Link

Navigates to an important page.
Set `fixed` to keep the link visible next to the menu button in narrow windows, and add an `icon` to display after the text.

<Canvas of={PageHeaderMenuLinkStories.MenuLink} />

<Controls of={PageHeaderMenuLinkStories.MenuLink} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

All our websites must start with the Page Header.
Consistent use helps people identify, navigate, and trust our digital channels.

The Page Header is the same on every page of the website, although full-screen pages (e.g. a video or map) may hide it.

### How to use

The Page Header must show the appropriate logo and brand name.
The navigation structure can be configured freely.

#### Logo

Use the correct logo: our main one, one for a sub-brand, or the English variation.
See [Logo](/docs/components-media-logo--docs) documentation for details.

The logo links to the homepage of the site it appears on.
This is a common convention that helps people navigate back to the homepage from any page of the website.

For websites with a brand name that feature the standard Amsterdam logo, only the emblem is shown on narrow screens.

#### Brand name

The City’s main website or that of a sub-brand must not display a brand name, as the logo already includes a wordmark.

All other websites must display the name of the brand or service next to the logo.
This helps people understand they are on a different website and that its navigation is separate from the main one.

An abbreviated brand name can be shown in narrow or medium-wide windows if the full name does not fit.

#### Inline menu

The menu to the right can contain a maximum of 5 items, including the menu button.
Labels should be short to help the menu fit on a single line whenever possible.
An [icon](/docs/brand-assets-icons--docs) can be added to a menu item if it helps clarify it.
Links move into the collapsible menu on narrow windows, unless they have the `fixed` prop.

#### Menu button

The ‘Menu’ button opens the collapsible menu.
It does not appear when the Page Header has no child content.
Use `noMenuButtonOnWideWindow` to hide the menu button on wide windows when there are only a few links.

#### Collapsible menu

This menu gets accessed through the menu button and offers much room for more links.
Use the `GridCellNarrowWindowOnly` subcomponent to contain links from the inline menu that disappear in narrow windows.
Don’t add whitespace to the Grid in the collapsible menu – its container already provides this.

If the collapsible menu contains [Headings](/docs/components-text-heading--docs), give them level 2 and a size of ‘level-3’.

#### Controlling the menu

By default the Page Header keeps track of whether the collapsible menu is open.
Set `defaultOpen` to have it open on the first render.

To control the menu yourself, pass `open` and update it from the `onOpenChange` callback.
This matters most in a single-page app: the Page Header stays mounted while navigating, so the menu would otherwise stay open after someone follows a link inside it.
Keep the open state in your own component and close it whenever the route changes:

{/* prettier-ignore */}
```tsx
function Header() {
  const { pathname } = useLocation() // The current route from your router
  const [menuOpen, setMenuOpen] = useState(false)
  const [previousPathname, setPreviousPathname] = useState(pathname)

  // Close the collapsible menu whenever the route changes
  if (pathname !== previousPathname) {
    setPreviousPathname(pathname)
    setMenuOpen(false)
  }

  return (
    <PageHeader onOpenChange={setMenuOpen} open={menuOpen}>
      {/* Collapsible menu content */}
    </PageHeader>
  )
}
```

## Examples

### With moving links

Links can move from the inline menu to the collapsible one on narrow windows.
A `MenuLink` is hidden by default on narrow windows.
Use `GridCellNarrowWindowOnly` to show that same link in the collapsible menu on narrow windows.

If you do not want the `MenuLink` to be hidden, use the `fixed` prop.

In this example, ‘English’ moves to the collapsible menu, while ‘Zoeken’ does not.

<Canvas of={PageHeaderStories.WithMovingLinks} />

### Without menu button on wide windows

If you only have a few links, you may not always need a collapsible menu.
Use `noMenuButtonOnWideWindow` to hide the menu button on wide windows.
On narrow windows, the menu button will still be visible,
so do not forget to add the links to the collapsible menu.

<Canvas of={PageHeaderStories.WithoutMenuButtonOnWideWindow} />

### Without menu button

In some cases, a collapsible menu might not be necessary.
If the Page Header has no `children`, the menu button will not appear.
Remember to use the `fixed` prop if you want the inline menu links to stay in place.

<Canvas of={PageHeaderStories.WithoutMenuButton} />

### With short brand name

For brand names that may not fit in a narrow window, a shorter form can be given.
Make sure the abbreviation is widely understood.

<Canvas of={PageHeaderStories.WithShortBrandName} />

### With custom logo link

The destination and accessible text of the logo link can be customized,
as well as the logo itself and its accessible name.

<Canvas of={PageHeaderStories.WithCustomLogoLink} />

### With custom texts

The visible text of the menu button, its accessible texts and the accessible navigation description can be customized.

<Canvas of={PageHeaderStories.WithCustomTexts} />

### With custom link component

Pass a custom link component to the `logoLinkComponent` prop to use your routing library for the logo link.
Here’s an example with the Link component of Next.js:

{/* prettier-ignore */}
```tsx
import { PageHeader } from "@amsterdam/design-system-react"
import NextLink from "next/link"

const LinkComponent = (props) => <NextLink {...props} />

return <PageHeader logoLinkComponent={LinkComponent} />
```

### With different branding

Websites for the City of Amsterdam **must** use one of our own logos and our menu icon.

Other organisations using this component can provide elements to display their own brand.
The image for the logo must be an svg, and its label should be ‘name of the organisation + logo’.
Set the appropriate values for the sizing tokens of [Logo](/docs/components-media-logo--docs).
A different icon for the menu button must be an svg as well.

<Canvas of={PageHeaderStories.WithDifferentBranding} />

## See also

- [Page](/docs/components-containers-page--docs) – contains the Page Header.
- [Page Footer](/docs/components-containers-page-footer--docs) – sits at the bottom of the Page.
- [Logo](/docs/components-media-logo--docs) – the logo shown in the Page Header.

<Meta of={ProgressListStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={ProgressListStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Subcomponents

Steps make up a Progress List.
A Step can contain Substeps, wrapped in the Substeps subcomponent, which has no props of its own.

### Step

Each step in the list has a heading, a status, and optionally collapsible content.

<Canvas of={ProgressListStepStories.Step} />

<Controls of={ProgressListStepStories.Step} />

### Substep

Marks a smaller activity within a step.
It takes a `status`, just like a Step, but has no heading.

<Canvas of={ProgressListSubstepStories.Substep} />

<Controls of={ProgressListSubstepStories.Substep} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Progress List to show the status of a multi-step process, such as the handling of a permit application or the phases of a construction project.

### How to use

Assign a status to each step: `completed` or `current`.
Steps without a status are considered _upcoming_.
Only one step may be `current`; all preceding steps must be `completed`.

Choose a `headingLevel` that fits the document outline.

Use on a white background only.

## Examples

### Controlled

Use `expanded` and `onToggle` on each step to let a parent component drive the expand/collapse state.
The example below keeps only one step open at a time.

<Canvas of={ProgressListStories.Controlled} />

### Collapsible

Set `collapsible` to `true` to let users expand and collapse the content of each step.
Current and upcoming steps then start expanded.
Completed ones are initially collapsed.
Use the `defaultExpanded` prop on a step to override the default behaviour.
The `onToggle` callback emits the expanded state whenever it changes.

<Canvas of={ProgressListStories.Collapsible} />

### With substeps

A step may contain a list of substeps.
They are visually subordinate to their parent step: their indicators are smaller, and they do not display a heading.

Don’t forget to set the `hasSubsteps` prop on the parent step.

<Canvas of={ProgressListStories.WithSubsteps} />

## Accessibility

The status is conveyed visually through both colour and an icon, and via screen reader text.
You can customize the screen reader text with `completedAccessibleText` and `currentAccessibleText` (defaults: ‘Klaar’ and ‘Bezig’).

## Usage guidelines

### When not to use

Do not position a Spotlight on the [Grid](/docs/components-layout-grid--docs).

### How to use

Use the entire width of the [Page](/docs/components-containers-page--docs) container.
Wrap its content in a Grid with extra large vertical padding.

Use any of the [highlight colours](/docs/brand-design-tokens-colour--docs) for the background.
The design system does not prescribe a meaning to any of these colours.
The default is purple.
Select [the correct colour](/docs/brand-design-tokens-colour--docs#pairing-foreground-with-background-colours) for text and links against the background you choose.

Find a fitting setup for the [amount and width of columns](/docs/pages-public-introduction--docs#how-to-size-the-grid-cells).

Use the `as` prop to render a meaningful HTML element: `as="section"` for a self-contained content area, `as="aside"` for supporting content.

## Examples

### Highlight content

Use a Spotlight to direct the user’s attention to the most important or actionable content on the page.

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/table.tokens.json";

import * as TableStories from "./Table.stories.tsx";
import * as TableCellStories from "./TableCell.stories.tsx";
import * as TableHeaderCellStories from "./TableHeaderCell.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={TableStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={TableStories} />

<Primary />

This component has no props to configure.

## Subcomponents

A Table is composed of a Caption, a Header containing Header Cells, a Body, an optional Footer, and Rows of Cells.
Caption, Header, Body, Footer, and Row have no props of their own; the example above shows each of them in place.

### Cell

Holds a single value within a row.
Use the `align` prop to align the content to the center or end of the cell.
Apply the same value to all cells in the column and the matching `Table.HeaderCell`.

<Canvas of={TableCellStories.Cell} />

<Controls of={TableCellStories.Cell} />

### Header Cell

Labels the column of values below it.
Use the `align` prop to match the alignment of the column’s cells.

<Canvas of={TableHeaderCellStories.HeaderCell} />

<Controls of={TableHeaderCellStories.HeaderCell} />

## Usage guidelines

### How to use

Use [Margin](/docs/utilities-css-margin--docs) or [Prose](/docs/utilities-css-prose--docs) to add vertical whitespace.

Add a caption so users can find and understand the Table without reading its data.
Use a [Heading](/docs/components-text-heading--docs) in it, at the level that fits the document outline.

To place content between the Heading and the Table, keep the Caption but hide it visually, then position the heading and content above the Table.
Do not use ARIA relations; they hurt the Table's semantics (see [this article](https://www.scottohara.me/blog/2019/04/19/tabled-tables.html)).

## Examples

### With footer and row headers

Use table headers to tell users what the rows and columns represent.
Use the scope attribute to help users of assistive technology distinguish between row and column headers.
Use `Table.Footer` for a summary row.

<Canvas of={TableStories.WithFooterAndRowHeaders} />

### With heading and description

When the table needs context – a source, a date, or reading instructions – place a heading and a small paragraph above it and hide the caption visually.

<Canvas of={TableStories.WithHeadingAndDescription} />

### With caption in figure

The context can be positioned below the table as well.
In this case, use a [Figure](/docs/components-media-figure--docs) and let the Table keep its Caption.

<Canvas of={TableStories.InFigure} />

## Accessibility

A Table caption creates the accessible name for the Table, announced by screen readers on every encounter.

## See also

- [Prose](/docs/utilities-css-prose--docs) – applies the recommended vertical spacing for editorial content.
- [Table Page](/docs/pages-internal-table-page--docs) – various templates for large data tables in internal websites.

<Meta of={TabsStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={TabsStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Subcomponents

The List groups the Buttons of all tabs; it has no props of its own and is visible in the example above.

### Button

Activates its tab.
Point the required `aria-controls` prop at the `id` of the corresponding Panel.

<Canvas of={TabsButtonStories.Button} />

<Controls of={TabsButtonStories.Button} />

### Panel

Holds the content of a tab.
Its `id` connects it to the Button that controls it.

<Canvas of={TabsPanelStories.Panel} />

<Controls of={TabsPanelStories.Panel} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use Tabs to let related content fragments share a space on the current page.
Each tab has a button that shows its content in a panel.

The content of each tab must be usable independent of the others.

### When not to use

Do not use Tabs to toggle between large amounts of primary content.
That would come down to navigating between pages.
In this context, use [Tab Navigation](/docs/components-navigation-tab-navigation--docs) to offer the user the benefits of links.

### How to use

Create a panel for each button.
Add an `aria-controls` attribute to each button and match its value to the `id` of the associated panel.

## Features

### Keyboard navigation

| Key            | Behaviour                                      |
| :------------- | :--------------------------------------------- |
| Enter or Space | Open or close the tab that has the focus       |
| Tab            | Go to the next element that can have focus     |
| Shift + Tab    | Go to the previous element that can have focus |
| Left arrow     | If the tabs have focus, go to the previous tab |
| Right arrow    | If the tabs have focus, go to the next tab     |
| Home           | If the tabs have focus, go to the first tab    |
| End            | If the tabs have focus, go to the last tab     |

## See also

- [Tab Navigation](/docs/components-navigation-tab-navigation--docs) – when each tab should navigate to its own page.

<Description of={AlertStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use an Alert if the message’s purpose matches one of the following:

- **Information** to bring attention to a message.
  This variation is blue and it is the default.
- **Success** to reassure that a process is complete.
  This variation is green.
- **Warning** when action is needed to prevent damage.
  This variation is orange.
- **Error** indicates an error has occurred.
  This variation is red.

### How to use

Place the Alert in a Grid Cell to create enough white space around it.

Important and urgent information is to be placed directly below the Page Header.
Examples: system outage or changes in the opening hours of a City Office.
This can be applied to the entire website or to a part of it.

Add a close button if the user should be able to dismiss the Alert.

## Examples

### Warning

Display a warning when user action is required.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Warning} />

### Error

In case of an error, use the red alert.
Provide the user with suggestions on alternative ways to achieve the goal.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Error} />

### Success

Announce the success of a significant action.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Success} />

### Information

An informative message can emphasize matters that are useful to follow.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Info} />

### With inline link

Include an inline link in the text to guide the user.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithInlineLink} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Show an Avatar for the user of the website, or to associate a person with a content item.

## Examples

### With image

The Avatar can also display a photo or other image for the person.
Make sure to scale the image down to around 100 pixels to prevent unnecessary data transfers.
The center of the image will be visible; provide a square image if possible.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.WithImage} />

### Fallback icon

A user icon displays if no label and image are provided.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.FallbackIcon} />

## Design

The Avatar contains 1 or 2 initial letters from the person’s full name, a picture, or a generic icon.

To personalize the Avatar, the user can be allowed to choose one of the [highlight colours](/docs/brand-design-tokens-colour--docs).
The default is purple.
The design system does not define a meaning to any of these background colours.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/character-count.tokens.json";

import * as CharacterCountStories from "./CharacterCount.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={CharacterCountStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={CharacterCountStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Only use a Character Count when there is a good reason for limiting the number of characters users can enter.
For example, if there is an indication that users are likely to enter more information than they need to.
Or when there is a legal or technical reason that means an entry must be no more than a certain number of characters.

### When not to use

If your users keep hitting the character limit imposed by the backend of your service then try to increase the limit rather than use a Character Count.

## Examples

### Error

When the length exceeds the maximum length, the colour of the text changes to red.

<Canvas of={CharacterCountStories.Error} />

## Features

Users will get updates at a pace that works best for the way they interact with the textarea.
This means:

- sighted users will see a count message that updates as they type;
- screen reader users will hear the count announcement when they stop typing.

This component does not restrict the user from entering information.
The user can enter more than the character limit, but are told they’ve entered too many characters.
This lets them type or copy and paste their full answer, then edit it down.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/checkbox.tokens.json";

import * as CheckboxStories from "./Checkbox.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={CheckboxStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={CheckboxStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use Checkboxes for one or multiple choices that do not exclude each other.
Each Checkbox operates independently of other Checkboxes in a list at the same hierarchical level.
Checking an additional Checkbox does not affect other selections in that list.

Use a Checkbox to answer a closed question if multiple answers are possible.

Use a group of Checkboxes to filter data on a page, in a menu, or within a component.

A Checkbox can also be used for bulk selection or deselection of an entire list of Checkboxes.
Still, it should be clear that the bulk selection Checkbox is at a different hierarchical level than the list being fully selected or deselected.

### When not to use

Use a [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) when a user can select only one option from a list.

### How to use

Wrap a list of Checkboxes in a Field Set with a legend describing what the list is about.
For example, if the Checkboxes are used to get answers to a question, the legend is the question.

### How to write

A label starts with a capital letter.
It does not have punctuation at the end if it is a single sentence, word, or fragment.
It is written in the first person when asking the user to agree to the terms and conditions.

## Examples

### Long label

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.LongLabel} />

### In a Field Set

Use a Field Set to group several Checkboxes with a legend, description and / or an Error Message.

Because of an [NVDA bug](https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/12718), we add the description text to the Field Set with `aria-labelledby`,
instead of `aria-describedby`.
Screen reader users will no longer be able to skip the description, but we think that is preferable to missing the description entirely.
The order of the `id`s is the order in which they are read by screen readers.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-labelledby` and `id` attributes from the Field Set.

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in descriptions. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-field--docs#no-rich-text).

Check [the Field Set docs](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.InAFieldSet} />

### In a Field Set with validation

A Field Set with Checkboxes can become invalid.
In this case, connect an Error Message to the Field Set.
Because of [the NVDA bug mentioned earlier](https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/12718),
we add the Error Message text to the label as well.
Add an `aria-labelledby` attribute to the Field Set and provide the `id` of Error Message as its value.
The order of the `id`s is the order in which they are read by screen readers.

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs#no-rich-text).

Check [the Field Set docs](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.InAFieldSetWithValidation} />

### With custom icon

Replace the icon with a custom version to use the Checkbox in a different theme or visual identity.
Use `ams-checkbox__rectangle`, `ams-checkbox__hover-indicator`, `ams-checkbox__checked-indicator`
and `ams-checkbox__indeterminate-indicator` classes in its SVG markup.
Websites for the City of Amsterdam must use the default icon.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.WithCustomIcon} />

## Design

A list of Checkboxes is vertically stacked to enhance readability and usability.

## See also

- [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) – when a user can select only one option from a list.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – groups several Checkboxes with a shared legend.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/date-input.tokens.json";

import * as DateInputStories from "./DateInput.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={DateInputStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={DateInputStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Date Input when the user must enter a calendar date and the date picker provided by the browser is appropriate.

### When not to use

When asking for a date that is easy to remember or find, like a birthday or passport expiration date,
use a Field Set with separate Text Inputs for day, month, and year.
This approach is easier to use than using a Date Input component.

For more information on this pattern, see the [gov.uk](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/date-input/) and [NL Design System](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/wanneer-welk-form-element/iedereen-kan-invullen) documentation.

Avoid disabling input fields.
They cause usability and accessibility problems.
Disabled fields are often skipped by screen readers.
This makes it hard for users who rely on assistive technologies to understand the form’s content.
They are not included in form submissions, which can lead to incomplete or missing data.

Alternatives:

1. Use the `readonly` attribute.
   This makes a field uneditable but keeps it accessible and included in form submissions.
2. Display data as plain text or within a non-input element like a `span` or `div`.
3. Use conditional logic to hide or show fields based on user interaction.
   This ensures all necessary fields are accessible and editable when needed.
4. Use a label or text to explain why a field is not editable if you must disable it temporarily.
   This helps the user understand the context.

### How to use

Wrap a Date Input in a Field to associate it with a Label, description, and Error Message.

## Examples

### Memorable date

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.MemorableDate} />

### Memorable date with validation

To show validation errors, add `invalid` and an [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) to the Field Set.
Make sure to connect the Error Message to the Field Set, otherwise this won’t be read by a screen reader.
Additionally, apply the `invalid` prop to the Text Inputs to visually indicate the error.
Only use the `invalid` prop on Text Inputs that have errors.
For example, only mark the ‘year’ input as invalid if the year is not provided.

See the [gov.uk](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/date-input/#error-messages) documentation on validation for this pattern.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.MemorableDateWithValidation} />

### Date and time

To let the user select a specific time on a date, use the `datetime-local` type.
Note that the control’s UI varies in general from browser to browser.

The value represents a local date and time, not necessarily the user’s local date and time.
In other words, the input allows any valid combination of year, month, day, hour, and minute – even if such a combination is invalid in the user’s local time zone.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.DateTime} />

### Invalid

Indicates that the input value does not meet the specified constraints.
An [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) must be displayed above the field.
To highlight the error even more, the parent [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) component’s `invalid` prop must also be set.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.Invalid} />

### Disabled

A field that can not (yet) be used is indicated with a grey border.
It will not respond to interactions, e.g. with the mouse or keyboard.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.Disabled} />

### In a Field

Use a Field to group a Date Input with a Label, description and / or an Error Message.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Date Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.InAField} />

### In a Field with validation

If the Date Input can become invalid, add an Error Message and its `id` to the `aria-describedby` attribute of the Date Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.InAFieldWithValidation} />

## Design

This component uses a native date input, which is styled differently in different browsers and operating systems.
Recreating the native functionality is quite difficult and prone to accessibility errors, which is why we’ve chosen not to do that.
This does mean that this component does not look identical on all browsers and operating systems.

## See also

- [Calendar](/docs/components-navigation-calendar--docs) – navigate between dates using a calendar view.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input with its Label, description, and Error Message.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – use with three Text Inputs for memorable dates instead of a Date Input.
- [Time Input](/docs/components-forms-time-input--docs) – the counterpart for entering a time.

<Meta of={DatePickerStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={DatePickerStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

**Note**: Some props are excluded from the controls panel: `mode`, `onChange`, and `value` are managed by the story’s state wrapper; `defaultMonth`, `isDateDisabled`, `maxDate`, and `minDate` have no suitable control widget for their type.
The `dir` and the navigation and accessible-name labels are read-only and follow `locale`, so the controls show a fully localised Date Picker; set them yourself in your app.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Date Picker when someone needs to choose a date or date range from a visible calendar, for example to book an appointment.

### When not to use

- Use a [Date Input](/docs/components-forms-date-input--docs) when the user knows the date and can type it into a form field.
- Use a [Calendar](/docs/components-navigation-calendar--docs) to browse content grouped by date, such as an events calendar.

### How to use

The Date Picker is a controlled component: it keeps no selection of its own.
Pass the current selection with `value` and update it in the `onChange` handler.

In the default single mode, `value` is a `Date` or `null` and `onChange` receives the picked date.
In range mode, set `mode="range"`; `value` is a `DateRange` (`{ start, end }`) and `onChange` receives the updated range.
The first pick sets the start, the second sets the end, and picking before the start begins a new range.

If you set `minDate` or `maxDate`, ensure the initial `value` falls within those bounds.
The component does not clamp or validate the incoming value.

#### Localisation

The Date Picker renders weekday names, the month caption, and the accessible date labels in the language of `locale`, which defaults to `nl-NL`.
It does not translate the rest: set `nextMonthButtonLabel`, `nextYearButtonLabel`, `previousMonthButtonLabel`, and `previousYearButtonLabel` in the same language, or they stay Dutch and screen readers announce a mix.
In range mode, also localise `rangeStartAccessibleName` and `rangeEndAccessibleName`; they are appended to the start and end dates when those are announced.
For right-to-left scripts such as Arabic, also add `dir="rtl"`.
Try the `locale` control above to preview each language; see the [Localisation developer guide](/docs/docs-developer-guide-localisation--docs) for the tested locales.

If your app uses Date Picker in multiple places with the same language, a small wrapper component avoids repeating these props:

```tsx
import type { DatePickerProps } from "@amsterdam/design-system-react";

import { DatePicker } from "@amsterdam/design-system-react";

const ArabicDatePicker = (props: DatePickerProps) => (
  <DatePicker
    dir="rtl"
    locale="ar-MA"
    nextMonthButtonLabel="الشهر التالي"
    nextYearButtonLabel="السنة التالية"
    previousMonthButtonLabel="الشهر السابق"
    previousYearButtonLabel="السنة السابقة"
    rangeEndAccessibleName="تاريخ النهاية"
    rangeStartAccessibleName="تاريخ البداية"
    {...props}
  />
);
```

## Design

The Date Picker is intentionally an inline component.
Finding the optimal date is a focused task for the user; placing it directly on the page makes it easier to use and gives it the space and attention it deserves.
If the layout truly has no room, placing the Date Picker inside a modal [Dialog](/docs/components-dialogs-dialog--docs) is an acceptable last resort.

## Examples

### Range

Set `mode="range"` to let users pick a start and end date.
The Date Picker itself does not communicate that a range is expected.
Use a label, heading, or instruction to make this clear.

The user picks the start date first.
A second click on a later date completes the range; clicking the same date completes a one-day range.
Clicking a date before the current start discards the selection and begins a new range from that date.
Any click after the range is complete starts over.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Range} />

### Disabled dates

Pass `isDateDisabled` to prevent selection of specific dates, such as ones that are unavailable.
Disabled dates remain reachable with the keyboard and are announced, but they cannot be selected.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.DisabledDates} />

### Within-month bounds

Use `minDate` and `maxDate` to bound the selectable period.
Dates outside the range cannot be selected, and the month and year navigation buttons stop at the edges of the range.

When the bounds fall within the current month, dates outside them appear disabled: they are struck through and cannot be selected, but remain reachable by keyboard.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.WithinMonthBounds} />

### Limited to one month

When `minDate` and `maxDate` align with month edges, all dates remain selectable.
Only the navigation buttons are disabled.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.LimitedToOneMonth} />

## Features

### Keyboard navigation

The day grid follows the [WAI-ARIA grid pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/).
Arrow keys move between days, Home and End jump to the start and end of the week, and Page Up and Page Down move between months; hold Shift for years.
Enter or Space selects the focused day.
Moving past the end of a month shows the adjacent month and keeps focus on the day.

## Accessibility

The grid takes its accessible name from the visible month caption, so screen readers announce which month is shown.
Each day button is labelled with its full date, including the weekday, so a day number is never read out of context.
In range mode, the start and end dates are announced as such; override `rangeStartAccessibleName` and `rangeEndAccessibleName` to localise these.

## See also

- [Date Input](/docs/components-forms-date-input--docs) – lets the user type a known date into a form field.
- [Calendar](/docs/components-navigation-calendar--docs) – displays content organised by date in a month view.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Show an Error Message above a form field that has a validation error.
For guidance and examples on using error messages in a form,
refer to the [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) and [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) documentation.

Read the documentation by [NL Design System](https://www.nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/foutmeldingen) and [Gov.uk](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-message/) for more information on the contents of error messages and when to show them.

### How to use

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message.
Some screen readers, like VoiceOver, skip over rich text when reading out descriptions.
For more information, see [NL Design System](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/descriptions/inhoud/).

Connect the Error Message to the input it describes through the input's `aria-describedby` attribute.

### How to write

Explain what went wrong and how to fix it.

## Examples

### Custom prefix

Error messages are automatically prefixed with a visually hidden text, the Dutch word ‘Invoerfout’.
This makes the error message more clear for screen reader users.
If you want to change this prefix, to support another language for example, you can use the `prefix` prop.

<Canvas of={ErrorMessageStories.CustomPrefix} />

### With custom icon

Replace the icon with another to use Error Message in a different theme or visual identity.
Websites for the City of Amsterdam must use the default icon.

<Canvas of={ErrorMessageStories.WithCustomIcon} />

## See also

- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input with its Label, description, and Error Message.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – wraps a group of inputs with a shared Error Message.
- [Invalid Form Alert](/docs/components-forms-invalid-form-alert--docs) – summarises all form errors at the top of the page.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Field to wrap a single input together with its Label, description, and Error Message.

### When not to use

Use [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) to wrap multiple inputs.

### How to use

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in descriptions.
Some screen readers, like VoiceOver, skip over rich text when reading out descriptions.
For more information, see [NL Design System](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/descriptions/inhoud/).

Connect each related element to the input through `aria-describedby` so screen readers announce them.

## Examples

### With description

A Field can have a description.
Make sure to connect this description to the input in the Field,
otherwise it won’t be read by a screen reader.
Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the input and provide the `id` of the describing element as its value.

<Canvas of={FieldStories.WithDescription} />

### With validation

A Field can indicate if the contained input has a validation error.
Use an [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) to describe the error.
Make sure to connect the Error Message to the input in the Field,
otherwise it won’t be read by a screen reader.
Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the input and provide the `id` of Error Message as its value.

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs#no-rich-text).

<Canvas of={FieldStories.WithValidation} />

### In a Field Set

Fields can be nested inside a Field Set.
Use the `inFieldSet` prop on the Labels of the Fields to show them in a lighter style.

<Canvas of={FieldStories.InAFieldSet} />

## Features

There’s no need to add white space between the children of a Field.
The component does this automatically.

## See also

- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – wraps multiple inputs.
- [Label](/docs/components-forms-label--docs) – names the input inside the Field.
- [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) – describes a validation error for the input.

components-forms-field-set--docs.content: {/* @license CC0-1.0 */} import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks"; import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable"; import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/field-set.tokens.json"; import * as FieldSetStories from "./FieldSet.stories.tsx"; <Description of={FieldSetStories} /> <Primary /> <Controls /> ## Usage guidelines ### When to use Group a collection of [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) buttons or [Checkboxes](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) into a Field Set. This allows them to share a label, description, and error message, while each option still has its own label. A Field Set can also express the relation between a group of inputs or other controls. For instance, you might want to group several text inputs into one Field Set when requesting an address or various parts of a name. ### When not to use Use a [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) to wrap a single input instead. ### How to use Mark a Field Set as `optional` only for a list of Radios or Checkboxes, and if selecting any option is not necessary. ## Examples ### With description A Field Set can have a description. Make sure to connect this description to the Field Set or a specific input, otherwise this won’t be read by a screen reader. Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the Field Set and provide the `id` of the describing element as its value. Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in descriptions. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-field--docs#no-rich-text). <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithDescription} /> ### With Hint A Field Set can indicate whether all of the inputs it contains are optional or required. Make sure to add `aria-required` to <em>all</em> form elements in the Field Set when they are required. <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithHint} /> ### With Validation A Field Set can indicate whether any of the inputs it contains has a validation error. Use an [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) to describe the error. Make sure to connect the Error Message to the correct input in the Field Set, otherwise it won’t be read by a screen reader. Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the input and provide the `id` of Error Message as its value. Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs#no-rich-text). <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithValidation} /> ### With Heading in Legend If the Field Set is the only content on the page, its Legend serves as the main heading as well. Set `legendIsPageHeading` to include an `h1` element to reflect this. <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithHeadingInLegend} /> ### With a nested Field Set A Field Set can be nested inside another Field Set. Use the `inFieldSet` prop to show the legend in a lighter style. <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithANestedFieldSet} /> ## Features There’s no need to add white space between the children of a Field Set. The component does this automatically. ## See also - [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input. - [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) – one of the inputs typically grouped in a Field Set. - [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) – one of the inputs typically grouped in a Field Set. ## Design tokens <DesignTokensTable tokens={tokens} />

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Title />

<Description of={FileInputStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a File Input when users need to attach one or more files from their device.

### How to use

Wrap a File Input in a Field to associate it with a Label and description.

## Examples

### Multiple files

Allow multiple files to be selected.
The label will update to show the number of files selected.

<Canvas of={FileInputStories.MultipleFiles} />

### Restrict file types

Limit the types of files that can be selected.
Some examples are `image/*`, `video/*`, or `audio/*`.
To limit to a specific file type, use the MIME type, such as `application/pdf`.

- [MDN File Input](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/file#limiting_accepted_file_types): More examples

<Canvas of={FileInputStories.RestrictFileTypes} />

### Disabled

<Canvas of={FileInputStories.Disabled} />

### In a Field

Use a Field component to group a File Input with a Label and possibly a description.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Text Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={FileInputStories.InAField} />

## Design

The filename label and button are displayed in the language of the browser and can vary between browsers and operating systems.

## See also

- [File List](/docs/components-forms-file-list--docs) – shows the files that the user has selected.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a File Input with its Label and description.

import { Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/invalid-form-alert.tokens.json";

import * as InvalidFormAlertStories from "./InvalidFormAlert.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={InvalidFormAlertStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={InvalidFormAlertStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Always show an Invalid Form Alert when there is a validation error, even if there’s only one.

### How to use

You must link the errors in the Invalid Form Alert to the answer they relate to.

For questions that require a user to answer using a single field, like a file upload, select, textarea or text input, link to the `id` of that field.

When a user has to enter their answer into multiple fields, such as day, month and year fields, link to the `id` of the first field that contains an error.
If you do not know which field contains an error, link to the `id` of the first field.

For questions that require a user to select one or more options from a list using Radios or Checkboxes, link to the `id` of the first Radio or Checkbox.

Put the Invalid Form Alert directly above the first question on the page.
Place it outside of the `<form>`-tag, [to make sure screen readers do not skip it](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/meerdere-stappen/#plaats-de-informatie-over-waar-de-gebruiker-is-in-de-stappen-boven-het-formulier).

The heading level of the Invalid Form Alert depends on where in the page it is placed; this may differ per page.

## Features

This component adds the error count to the document title,
in line with [GOV.UK guidelines for informing users about validation errors](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/validation/#how-to-tell-the-user-about-validation-errors).

This component receives focus the first time it gets displayed on a page.
This allows keyboard users to quickly navigate to the errors in the form.
It also scrolls the component into view if it isn’t already.
Note: this functionality has been disabled on this page, to prevent unexpected focus behaviour.

## See also

- [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) – the per-field message linked from the Invalid Form Alert.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input with its Label, description, and Error Message.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – wraps a group of inputs with a shared Error Message.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Always associate a form element (such as an `input` or `textarea`) with a Label.

### How to use

Set `optional` to `true` if the input is not required.
Use `hint` to show a custom hint text.

## Examples

### Optional

Use the `optional` prop to indicate that the user doesn’t need to fill in the field to submit the form.

<Canvas of={LabelStories.Optional} />

### With hint

Use the `hint` prop to either customize the text for the optional property or provide another type of remark.

Note: ensure the hint meets [language level B1](https://www.amsterdam.nl/schrijfwijzer/heldere-taal-basis-onze-huisstijl/).
For the same reason, the default hint text in Dutch is ‘niet verplicht’, not ‘optioneel’.

<Canvas of={LabelStories.WithHint} />

### With Heading

If the parent Field is the only content on the page, its Label serves as the main heading as well.
Set `isPageHeading` to include an `h1` element to reflect this.

<Canvas of={LabelStories.WithHeading} />

### In a Field Set

When a Label is used in a Field inside a Field Set, use the `inFieldSet` prop to show it in a lighter style.

<Canvas of={LabelStories.InAFieldSet} />

## See also

- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input together with its Label.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – uses a legend instead of a Label to name a group of inputs.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/password-input.tokens.json";

import * as PasswordInputStories from "./PasswordInput.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={PasswordInputStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={PasswordInputStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use this component when the input requires sensitive information, like passwords or PINs.
It ensures that the input is not readable by others who might be looking at the screen.

### How to use

Consider setting the following attributes:

1. Allow the user’s password manager to automatically fill the password through `autocomplete="current-password"`.
   When asking for a new password, use `autocomplete="new-password"` instead.
2. Do not add a `minlength` attribute to ensure passwords meet a minimum length requirement.
   This would prematurely indicate an error to the user – while they are still typing.
3. Do not add a `maxlength` attribute either.
   Users will not get any feedback when their text input has been truncated, e.g. after pasting from a password manager.
4. If the password is a numeric PIN, add `inputmode="numeric"`.
   Devices with virtual keyboards then switch to a numeric keypad layout which makes entering the password easier.

Follow the [guidelines for asking for passwords](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/passwords/) of the GOV.UK Design System.

Wrap a Password Input in a Field to associate it with a Label, description, and Error Message.

## Examples

### Size

Match the width of the input to the expected length of its content.
Use the `size` attribute for this.
The input won’t grow beyond the width of its container.

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.Size} />

### In a Field

Use a Field to group a Password Input with a Label, description and / or an Error Message.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Password Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.InAField} />

### In a Field with validation

If the Password Input can become invalid, add an Error Message and its `id` to the `aria-describedby` attribute of the Password Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.InAFieldWithValidation} />

## Features

The characters entered are hidden, represented by squares.

This component sets `autocorrect="off"` and `spellcheck="false"` to stop browsers automatically changing user input.
Passwords shouldn’t be checked for spelling or grammar.
This may also prevent posting the password to third-party plugins.
These props cannot be overridden.

## See also

- [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs) – for non-sensitive single-line text.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a Password Input with its Label, description, and Error Message.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Meta of={RadioStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={RadioStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Radio when the user must select exactly one option from a list.

### When not to use

Use a [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) when a user can select more than 1 option from a list.

Do not assume that users will know how many options they can select based on the visual difference between Radios and Checkboxes alone.
If needed, add a hint explaining this, for example, ‘Select one option’.

### How to use

Order Radios alphabetically by default.
In some cases, it can be helpful to order them from most-to-least common options.
For example, you could order options for ‘Where do you live?’ based on population size.
However you should do this with extreme caution as it can reinforce bias.
If in doubt, order alphabetically.

Do not check a Radio initially.
This prevents users from leaving the question unanswered.
It also increases the chance of submitting a wrong answer.

Wrap a list of Radios in a Field Set so they share a legend and any description or Error Message.

### How to write

Labels should be concise.
Try to keep labels shorter than 4 words.

## Examples

### In a Field Set

Use a Field Set to group several Radios with a legend, description and / or an Error Message.

Add `role="radiogroup"` to the Field Set to have it explicitly announced as a radio group (the default role is just ‘group’).
The ‘radio group’ role also allows using `aria-required` on Field Set; that isn’t allowed for the ‘group’ role.
Even so, always set `aria-required` on the individual Radios as well to ensure that screen readers can read it.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Field Set.

Check [the Field Set docs](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.InAFieldSet} />

### In a Field Set with validation

A Field Set with a Radio group can become invalid.
In this case, connect an Error Message to the Field Set.
Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the Field Set and provide the `id` of Error Message as its value.

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs#no-rich-text).

Check [the Field Set docs](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.InAFieldSetWithValidation} />

### With custom icon

Replace the icon with a custom version to use the Radio in a different theme or visual identity.
Use `ams-radio__circle`, `ams-radio__hover-indicator` and `ams-radio__checked-indicator` classes in its SVG markup.
Websites for the City of Amsterdam must use the default icon.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.WithCustomIcon} />

## See also

- [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) – when a user can select more than one option.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – groups several Radios with a shared legend.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/search-field.tokens.json";

import * as SearchFieldStories from "./SearchField.stories.tsx";
import * as SearchFieldButtonStories from "./SearchFieldButton.stories.tsx";
import * as SearchFieldInputStories from "./SearchFieldInput.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={SearchFieldStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={SearchFieldStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Subcomponents

A Search Field always combines an Input and a Button, as the example above shows.

### Input

The text input of the Search Field.
Its visually hidden `label` describes the field for screen readers.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldInputStories.Input} />

<Controls of={SearchFieldInputStories.Input} />

### Button

Submits the search.
It renders an icon-only Button whose `children` provide the accessible name.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldButtonStories.Button} />

<Controls of={SearchFieldButtonStories.Button} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Search Field where the user needs to search through the content of the page or website.

### How to use

You can use `autofocus` to place focus directly on a search field when the user arrives on a page.
However, use this feature with caution, as it can have negative consequences:

- For screen reader users, this may result in skipping important content above the search field.
- On smaller devices, the use of `autofocus` may automatically scroll the page to the search field, potentially causing users to miss previous content.
- On touchscreen devices, this can trigger the keyboard to appear immediately, hiding important content.

Use `autofocus` only if the search field is at the beginning of a page and there are no other elements on a page that a user might want to interact with first.

For more information: [Accessibility Tips: Be Cautious When Using Autofocus](https://www.boia.org/blog/accessibility-tips-be-cautious-when-using-autofocus)

Provide a label that describes the purpose of the search.

## Examples

### With placeholder

A Search Field can have a placeholder text.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldStories.WithPlaceholder} />

### Controlled component

By default, the search field is not managed by React but by the browser.
However, it can be controlled by React.
If you enter a value in this search field and use the search Button or the Enter key, you will receive a notification.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldStories.Controlled} />

## Features

Users can initiate a search by using the search button or the Enter key.

Both `autocomplete` and `spellcheck` are turned off by default.
These features can be disruptive for a user searching for part of a word, and `autocomplete` may interfere with an Autosuggest component.

## Accessibility

The component uses `role="search"` for the search landmark role.

## See also

- [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs) – for free-text input that isn’t a search.

## Subcomponents

Provide the choices of the Select with Option subcomponents, and group related choices with a Group.
They render the native `<option>` and `<optgroup>` elements and accept their standard attributes only.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Select when the user must pick one option from a list that is too long to display as Radios.

### When not to use

Avoid adding functionality to allow selecting multiple options.
Multi select is harder to use on desktop as they require the user to hold down the `Ctrl` or `Cmd` key while clicking on the options.
It is recommended to use checkboxes instead.

### How to use

Wrap a Select in a Field to associate it with a Label, description, and Error Message.

## Examples

### Grouped

Use the `Select.Group` component to group options.
The component requires a `label` attribute.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Grouped} />

### Invalid

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Invalid} />

### Disabled

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Disabled} />

### In a Field

Use a Field to group a Select with a Label, description and / or an Error Message.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Select.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.InAField} />

### In a Field with validation

If the Select can become invalid, add an Error Message and its `id` to the `aria-describedby` attribute of the Select.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.InAFieldWithValidation} />
